tagline.text: A waterfall dropping about 20 m in the mountains of Catarman, Camiguin

location.label: Location
location.text: Mountain road in Barangay Mainit, Catarman, Camiguin

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May, the relatively dry months (early morning recommended)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,000 (entrance fee plus scooter rental or tricycle transport)

children.text: Tuasan Falls is a waterfall about 20 m high in the hills of Catarman, on the western side of Camiguin Island. It is only a 1–2 minute walk from the parking area, and you can swim in the rock pools below. It makes an easy half-day stop on a trip around the island.

Tuasan Falls sits in the hills of Barangay Mainit in Catarman, on the western side of Camiguin Island. A single 20 m ribbon of water slides down a rock face between green forest and lands in a clear pool, a simple but refreshing waterfall. If Katibawasan Falls, the island's best-known waterfall on the north side, tends to be crowded with tourists, Tuasan is comparatively quiet, and one visitor reports having it almost to himself early in the morning. The falls are described as lying along the Looc River, and the map sources' coordinates, around 9.18°N and 124.68°E, agree within about 100 m.

Below the falls are two rock pools in sequence. The first is where the water lands directly, and the water then spills like a small waterfall into the second pool. The edges have been widened to make it easier for visitors to get in, though the place is described as keeping its natural look. One review says the water is shoulder deep with no strong currents, while another says the current near the falls is strong and hard to stand in, so check the current for yourself before going close to the base.

At the entrance there is reportedly a ticket office, a large parking lot, a small shop selling snacks, restrooms and a place to change. From the parking lot, a paved path leads to the falls in about a 1–2 minute walk, so children and adults alike can get there easily. There are also reports of a lifeguard next to the falls. Facilities and operation can change, so check the latest information before you visit. The entrance fee is given as ₱50 in Catarman's tourism information but ₱75 in recent travel reviews, so the two disagree. The falls are said to be managed by the Camiguin provincial government, so go by the price board on site. Opening hours are given as from 7 AM or 8 AM until 5 PM.

The way there is part of the appeal. Riding a scooter along the mountain road through villages and forest lets you enjoy Camiguin's scenery. However, some stretches are steep and often wet from frequent rain, so choose the safer option if you are not confident driving. Camiguin is nicknamed the "Island Born of Fire" because it is a small island with many volcanoes, and a short way up from the coast you find waterfalls, cold springs and hot springs. Tuasan Falls is one of the watercourses shaped by this volcanic terrain, and it suits an itinerary built around beaches and hot springs when you want to add a swim in the forest.

blocks.title: A single drop of about 20 m

children.text: The water pours down the rock face in one drop. The surroundings are forested and the water is clear, so it is good for photos. After rain the flow increases and the water can turn cloudy.

The first pool, where the falls land, and a second pool below it are arranged in tiers. Children can play in the lower pool while confident swimmers go to the upper one. Depth varies by spot, so ease in slowly from the edge at first.

blocks.title: A 1–2 minute walk to the falls

children.text: A paved path runs from the parking lot to the falls. It is easy to reach even if you have difficulty walking or are carrying a child.

A lifeguard post beside the falls, a ticket office, a snack shop and restrooms are reported. Facilities are basic, so bring your own towel and a change of clothes. A small shop near the entrance sells coconuts and drinks, which is nice for resting after a swim.
The scooter ride along the mountain road to the falls is itself a highlight. Camiguin is small enough to circle in a day, so the falls fit easily into a round-the-island route.

Instead of the steep mountain road, there is a safer route that follows the coastal circumferential road into Mainit. Along it you pass sights such as the Sunken Cemetery, old Spanish church ruins, the Bura Soda Water Pool and the Sto. Niño Cold Spring.

items.title: Morning falls trip
items.subtitle: About a half day from Mambajao

children.text: Rent a scooter in Mambajao or charter a tricycle and set off. Rent the scooter with a full tank of fuel.
Head to the falls over the mountain road. Going directly takes about 30 minutes. Slow down if the road is wet.
Arrive at the falls and buy your ticket. It is quiet in the morning, which is nice.
Swim in the pools and take photos. The current is strong close to the falls, so follow the lifeguard's instructions.
Change clothes, have a snack and rest.
Come back down to the coastal circumferential road for lunch and your next stop.
Times are examples and vary with road and weather conditions. Return time and fuel conditions for scooters differ by rental shop, so check beforehand.

items.title: Western island loop
items.subtitle: A day via the Mainit route

children.text: Follow the circumferential road west from Mambajao. This is the route to choose if you want the safer way.
Snorkel and take photos at the Sunken Cemetery and the Guiob church ruins.
Stop at the Bura Soda Water Pool or the Sto. Niño Cold Spring.
Have lunch, then head up from Mainit toward Tuasan Falls.
Swim and rest at the falls, then come back down before sunset.
This route takes longer but avoids the steep mountain road.
Flights from Manila to Camiguin Airport (CGM) may or may not be available depending on the period. Check the airline's notices for current service.
A widely used option is to fly into Cagayan de Oro (CGY), travel overland to Balingoan port and take a boat to the island. Check travel time and fares locally.
Ferry service can be affected by weather, so check the schedule in advance.
A scooter is the most widely recommended option. Reviewers report renting one in Mambajao for about ₱350~400 a day, and you should check whether it must be returned with a full tank.
Reviewers report about ₱200 one way by tricycle. Negotiate the waiting time and the return fare in advance.
Some reviews give about ₱40~50 for a jeepney, while others say there is no public transport. Check locally.
Some operators include the falls in an island tour. Check when booking that the falls are on the itinerary.

The direct route from Mambajao takes about 30 minutes, but the mountain road is steep, so allow plenty of time if it is your first visit. The route that enters Mainit along the coastal road takes longer.
Parts of the mountain road are steep and slippery after rain, so if you are not confident driving, take the Mainit route.

Camiguin's relatively dry months, November–May, are best for the falls. In rainy periods the flow grows and is more powerful, but the water can turn muddy and the road can be slippery. Conditions change a lot around days of rain, so ask at your lodging whether it rained the day before.
Morning is the best time of day. One reviewer went early and had the falls almost to himself. Groups and local families arrive in the afternoon, so go early if you want quiet.
Afternoon downpours are common, so bring a raincoat and try to finish the falls in the morning. After heavy rain, avoid swimming for safety and change your plans.

Most lodging on Camiguin is clustered around Mambajao and along the coastal circumferential road. Tuasan Falls is about 30 minutes by vehicle from there, so staying near Mambajao makes it easy to reach the falls, White Island, the Sunken Cemetery and more. Reviewers sometimes recommend a beach resort near Mambajao. Rooms fill up early on weekends and holidays, so check in advance.

There is said to be a small shop at the falls entrance selling coconuts and snacks. For lunch, eat in Mambajao or at a restaurant along the coastal road. Camiguin is known for seafood and sweet pastel buns, so try them along the way. We suggest visiting the falls first, then relaxing at a beach or hot spring in the afternoon.
Going early in the morning is the quietest and gives the best photos.
If you go by scooter, bring your license and a helmet, and slow down after rain.
Bring a quick-dry towel, a change of clothes and a dry bag.
The rocks are slippery, so aqua shoes or Crocs-style shoes are useful.
Reviewers say sunscreen is expensive locally and fakes have been sold, so buy it before you come.
Carry cash in pesos. Entrance fees and snacks are easier to pay in cash.
Combine it with Katibawasan Falls and the Sunken Cemetery on the same day for an efficient loop through the west and north.
If the steep mountain road worries you, choose the Mainit route.
ATMs may be scarce on the island, so withdraw cash in Mambajao beforehand.
Putting wet clothes in a separate plastic bag keeps the rest of your scooter luggage dry after the falls.
Reviewers say the current directly below the falls is strong and hard to stand in. Follow the lifeguard's instructions, and do not swim right after heavy rain.
After rain, the mountain road and the rocks around the falls are very slippery.
Parts of the scooter route are steep and wet. Beginners should consider the Mainit route or a tricycle.
Entrance fees and hours differ from source to source. Check the latest price locally.
Have a companion or the lifeguard watch your belongings and do not leave valuables while you swim.
Children must always be watched by an adult at their side.
When renting a scooter, photograph any existing scratches and check insurance and liability for accidents.
A volcanic island with Tuasan Falls. You can cover hot springs, waterfalls and beaches in one or two days.

blocks.title: Sunken Cemetery & Guiob Church Ruins, Camiguin

children.text: A sight along the Mainit-side circumferential road where you can see an old cemetery and church ruins that sank into the sea.
A sandbar island in the sea off northern Camiguin. Plan it for a different day from the falls.
